source.title: From Local Evidence to Safety Verdicts: Causal Tracing in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Faezeh Dehghan Tarzjani; Mevan Wijewardena; A. Romanus; Sampad Mohanty

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses activation patching and a leave-one-out safety direction to steer and read out VLM safety-classifier verdicts. It does not test refusal behavior or whether the refusal direction from the claim mediates refusal.
record.gate_note: The measured behavior is a binary safe/unsafe classification of image–prompt combinations from next-token logits, not a chat model refusing a harmful user request. The study estimates safe-minus-unsafe directions for this classification task; it does not use the harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction as a refusal intervention. Related findings are recorded as none for the listed claim versions. Cited results about refusal directions are background only. No result is reported for an attack suppressing the direction, robustness training, or reasoning models.
record.test_reason: The study measures a VLM safety classifier's 'Yes/No' safe/unsafe verdict, read from next-token logits under an explicit classifier instruction. It does not measure refusal of user requests. Its safe-minus-unsafe difference-in-means direction, added at the final token, borrows the method of the original work. It is applied to a related but different construct, safety classification of image-prompt combinations, with no refusal rate, ablation or weight edit. So no claim version is tested; the findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find a recurring handoff: changed input positions matter earlier, the final token later. Leave-one-out directions influence the late verdict, and linear readouts predict the model's own decisions, including mistakes. A readable verdict is not a correct safety judgment, and patching does not show the selected states are necessary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation patching and a leave-one-pair-out safe-minus-unsafe direction at the final input token for VLM safe/unsafe classification. It does not measure refusal, use a harmful-minus-harmless instruction mean for refusal, ablate across all layers and positions, or test refusal induction. The paper presents its own controlled multimodal analysis, not a replication of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by decoder layer and intervention site; the text and image subsets have different classification instructions; results are reported by model, subset, direction, and intervention strength. Text tokenwise analyses require tokenizer alignment. The readout is standardized in the main analysis; an unstandardized image-subset check has similar handoff-layer AUCs but lower last-layer AUC.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-token patching becomes effective late, at handoff layers 45/19/26 (text) and 44/18/26 (image). Patching the changed text token or the masked visual region is effective earlier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLM safe/unsafe classification, causal influence on the verdict shifts from the changed input evidence to the final-token state over decoder depth.

fits_no_version.finding: A leave-one-out safe-minus-unsafe mean direction at the final token steers the classifier verdict, sometimes overshooting. It reads out the model's own verdict (AUC 0.94-1.0 at handoff) better than dataset labels (0.75-0.94) and beats random directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means safety-verdict direction in VLMs is causally effective and linearly readable from late layers, tracking the model's decision including its errors; this is about classification, not refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Counterfactual-change geometry shows excess cross-model alignment of 0.34-0.50 after the handoff. The leading principal direction captures 49-85% of image change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer safety-verdict changes have partly shared across-example structure across VLMs, without demonstrated direction transfer.

record.problems: The benchmark is small and deliberately controlled, with 57 text and 60 image pairs, and only three models are tested. Intervention samples include only pairs each model correctly distinguishes, so patching results need not generalize to misclassified inputs. The experiments use subset-specific binary classification instructions rather than open-ended responses. Patching shows that selected states can influence the verdict, not that they are necessary or uniquely responsible. For image pairs, 46 of 60 have pixel differences outside the intended edit mask, and the vision encoder can propagate information beyond it. The authors also state that a readable verdict need not be a correct safety judgment.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows omitted. Numerical values from layerwise plots without separately stated numerical descriptions were not transcribed as exact values.

untested.parts: No refusal behaviour is measured. There is no harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction, no ablation removing refusal, and no addition inducing refusal. The steering acts on a classifier verdict only.
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
No jailbreak or attack analysis, and no adversarial training against ablation.
Leading-principal-direction concentration (49-85%) is measured for image-counterfactual change vectors, not for refusal dimensionality.
The readout tracks the model's verdict better than dataset labels. But no separate refusal decision is measured, so harm versus refusal is not separated.
Cross-model kernel alignment of change vectors is measured; authors state no direction transfer is shown. There is no language or base-to-instruct transfer.
No comparison of training procedures or stages.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test classification is accepted; T6 is a defensible alternative, since the paper only cites Arditi et al. and adapts its difference-in-means steering to a classification verdict. The reverse-direction handoff layers (45/19/25 text, 45/20/25 image) are not rowed but bear on no version. Row states are relative to the paper's own measures, since all rows link to none.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal behavior, refusal-direction ablation, or addition-induced refusal is measured. The interventions target safe/unsafe classifier verdicts on VLM inputs.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No attack that suppresses a refusal direction and no training against its ablation are evaluated.
The paper measures concentration of image-counterfactual change vectors along a principal direction, not whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
The paper compares the model's safety-classifier verdict with dataset annotations, but does not separately probe harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Cross-model alignment of counterfactual changes is measured, but no direction is transferred between models; no language, base-to-instruct, or other claimed transfer is tested.
No refusal training procedure or training-stage comparison is tested.
No reasoning model or refusal after reasoning is tested.

rows.operation_detail: Patch the differing text token between safe and unsafe runs and measure recovery across decoder layers.

rows.measure: Normalized recovery at the differing token
rows.value: Recovery begins near one in earlier layers, decreases through the middle layers, and falls to approximately zero around a model-specific transition
rows.uncertainty: One sample standard deviation across eligible examples is shown in figures; numeric values not stated here
